mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.5% in a 3-month window, it signals economic weakness that triggers a flight to safety, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicate economic overheating that prompts aggressive central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and CPIAUCSL are rising, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, accelerating GDP growth (GDPC1) signals strong economic momentum that supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods, or the Rank IC for GDPC1 growth rate is below 0.03 in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) consistently indicates robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months with PAYEMS growth above 100k, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105 in a 3-month window, it signals a manufacturing slowdown that reduces corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 105, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decreases in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a tightening monetary policy during labor strength, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime, rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals central bank intervention that increases equity discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of high-inflation periods, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL growth is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
